scenes.title: J. Ridley Stroop timing 1935 Nashville students on the 100-item Solid Color Card (63.3s) vs Mismatched Color-Word Card (110.3s)
scenes.era: 1935, Jesup Psychological Laboratory, George Peabody College, Nashville

layout.description: Sunlit 1935 wood-trimmed university psychology classroom with two large white easel test boards side by side — Card 1 displaying neat rows of solid red, blue, green, brown, and purple color squares, and Card 2 displaying 100 bold color words printed in clashing inks ('RED' in blue, 'BLUE' in green, 'GREEN' in red) — beside an oak desk holding an analog laboratory stopwatch.

positions.who: J. Ridley Stroop (mannequin in 1935 three-piece tweed vest suit and tie)
positions.where: standing beside the twin easel boards clicking a chrome laboratory stopwatch as the student moves from Card 1 (63.3s) to Card 2 (110.3s)
breezing smoothly down Card 1's solid color squares, then leaning forward, blinking, and catching their own tongue halfway through Card 2's mismatched color words
positions.facing: seated facing the two test boards

props.name: 1935 10×10 Solid Color Patch Card vs Mismatched Color-Word Card
props.period_detail: twin crisp white cardstock grids showing solid color squares (63.3 s) beside incongruent color words like RED in blue ink (110.3 s)
props.physical_behavior: lets viewers experience the exact interference instantly on screen

props.name: chrome 1935 laboratory stopwatch & '+47.0s (+74.3%)' chalkboard tally
props.period_detail: analog stopwatch on oak desk paired with neat chalk timings for Experiment 1 (+5.6%) vs Experiment 2 (+74.3%)

actions.verb_sequence: points briskly across solid color squares finishing in 63.3 seconds -> shifts to the mismatched Color-Word board and stammers mid-row as mouth starts forming the printed word instead of the ink
clicks the stopwatch at 110.3 seconds and chalks '+47.0 sec (+74.3%)' on the board

reactions.reaction: laughs in disbelief at being unable to ignore four simple letters

scenes.wardrobe: 1935 American collegiate wear: wool vest suit with necktie; collegiate knit cardigan and pleated trousers.
scenes.recognition_hook: Solid color squares take 63 seconds; print the wrong color word in that exact same ink and every single human in the room slows to 110 seconds.

key_visual.description: a 1935 researcher with a stopwatch beside two tabletop/easel cardstock grids comparing solid color squares (63.3s) and mismatched ink color words like RED in blue ink (110.3s)

scenes.title: Preschooler vs Professor: When Not Knowing How to Read Wins

layout.description: Bright testing table where a 4-year-old pre-reader and a bespectacled professor race on mismatched color cards.

positions.where: pointing cheerfully and naming every ink color without a millisecond of hesitation
squinting and stumbling as automatic reading hijacks every word

props.name: identical incongruent Stroop cards
props.period_detail: produce zero interference before literacy and massive lag after literacy
props.physical_behavior: proves reading automaticity is the culprit

actions.verb_sequence: rattles off ink colors effortlessly -> Professor hesitates on the exact same row

reactions.reaction: smiles recording developmental proof of automaticity

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s child overalls and professor tweed jacket.
scenes.recognition_hook: Before first grade teaches you to read, the Stroop trap has zero power over your brain.

scenes.title: Foreign-Script Fluency Detector

layout.description: Clean desk displaying color cards in Cyrillic, Kanji, and English scripts.

positions.where: breezing through unfamiliar script colors then lagging noticeably on the script they secretly read fluently

props.name: multi-script color-word cards
props.period_detail: only trigger interference in scripts wired to automatic meaning

actions.verb_sequence: flips unfamiliar script card (fast) -> flips fluent language card (instant 200-ms vocal lag)

scenes.recognition_hook: You can claim you don't read a language — until the word 'RED' in blue ink betrays your tongue.

scenes.title: Human-Factors Design: Never Paint 'STOP / DELETE' Green
scenes.era: Modern UX & aviation cockpit design studio

layout.description: Sunlit interface workstation comparing a clashing green 'DELETE' button with an aligned red 'DELETE' / green 'CONFIRM' pair.

positions.where: replacing Stroop-clashing UI buttons with color-aligned controls

props.name: aligned vs clashing UI button mockups
props.period_detail: eliminates Stroop error spikes under cockpit or hospital fatigue

actions.verb_sequence: swaps clashing green-Delete button for aligned red-Delete -> error bar drops to near zero

scenes.recognition_hook: Good design aligns color with meaning so tired humans never fight a Stroop war at 2 a.m.
